findings.title: Sub-domain classification inverts the business model

evidence.differentiation: **yes** — the premium customers pay for; a new entrant would need both the depot network and the planning know-how
no — required, and two vendors already do it well

findings.impact: Invoicing is 44.7% of tables and 51.2% of attributes and is built as a full domain model, while the one capability the business calls differentiating (Consolidation) is 6.6% of tables and is classified 'supporting'. Investment follows the classification, so this misdirects the build.

findings.title: Zero failure or compensation events — the model is happy-path only

known_failure_paths_from_discovery: overbooked container means a shipment is bumped (hotspot 1 / stated rule)
partner carrier refuses a sealed container (hotspot 3, unowned)
Invoicing declares CreditNote + DunningCase aggregates, so credits and non-payment exist in reality but emit no events

findings.impact: Every reversal path is undesigned. Teams will invent incompatible compensation logic per context, and the two hotspots that already cost money stay unowned.

findings.title: The same word carries different meanings AND the same type name carries different shapes

consignment.definition: The goods a customer hands over as one unit
A billable line on an invoice

evidence.discovery_hotspot: Hotspot 2: 'Finance and operations use "consignment" differently — a billable line vs a physical stack of pallets'

findings.impact: The discovery session logged this as an open hotspot; the model then encoded both meanings instead of resolving them, and reused ConsignmentLine as a cross-context type with two incompatible attribute sets. Sharing that type silently drops fields.

findings.title: The capacity invariant is written where it cannot be enforced (check-then-act across a boundary)

evidence.invariant: Consolidation: 'A container's committed volume must never exceed its capacity'
booking_invariant: A booking may only be confirmed once its capacity has been reserved
evidence.discovery_hotspot: Hotspot 1: 'Two shipments were committed to the same container slot in March; nobody agrees where the check should have happened'
evidence.business_impact_stated: an overbooked container means a shipment is bumped and the Guaranteed Consolidation promise is broken

findings.impact: Booking reads remaining capacity synchronously from Consolidation, then commits in its own transaction. Two concurrent bookings both read space and both commit. This is the exact March incident, and the model reproduces the design that caused it rather than fixing it. It also directly breaks the +18% premium the revenue stream depends on.

findings.title: The customs-before-handover rule is owned by a context that cannot enforce it, and the confirmed timeline violates it

evidence.rule: A shipment cannot be handed to a carrier before its declaration is submitted
evidence.contradiction: the timeline both sides confirmed puts handover TWO events before the declaration it is supposed to wait for

findings.impact: Routing has no aggregate, no invariant, and no relationship to Customs — it cannot check anything. Meanwhile the confirmed event order contradicts the confirmed rule and nobody reconciled them. Build this as written and you ship a compliance violation on the happy path.

findings.title: The declared shared identifier does not exist in two of the four contexts that supposedly share it, and no event carries it

evidence.context_map_claim: `ShipmentRef` value object shared by Booking, Consolidation, Customs, Invoicing (sharing level: Building Blocks)

reality.consolidation: ABSENT — never appears in this model
reality.invoicing: ABSENT — never appears in this model

evidence.upstream_of_customs: Consolidation, whose events carry containerId / bookingId / fillRate — never shipmentRef

findings.impact: Customs keys its Declaration on shipmentRef, but nothing upstream ever emits one. There is no end-to-end correlation key from a booking to its declaration to its invoice, so the chain cannot be joined at runtime and cannot be audited after an incident.

findings.title: Invoicing's only invariant references a field that does not exist on the entity

invariant: An invoice line must reference a cleared declaration
evidence.gap: InvoiceLine has no declarationId, no shipmentRef, no link of any kind to Customs

findings.impact: 'An invoice line must reference a cleared declaration' is unimplementable as modelled. Either the invariant is aspirational or the entity is wrong — and it is the one rule standing between the company and invoicing for uncleared goods.

findings.title: Context map records direction only — no integration pattern on any edge
findings.impact: 'upstream/downstream' fixes no contract. Nothing says which side translates, who may break whom, or whether an ACL exists. The one place a pattern IS named (Shared Kernel in context-map.md) is contradicted by both model.yaml files, which call the same pair upstream/downstream.

findings.title: The premium that justifies the whole product is not in the model

evidence.revenue_stream: Guaranteed Consolidation premium (+18% of forwarding fee) — promises a departure slot even on a partly-filled container
evidence.stated_rule_unmodelled: The premium is charged whether or not the container ends up full (finance analyst) — no matching invariant in Invoicing
invoicing_invariants: An invoice line must reference a cleared declaration
evidence.short_horizon_goal: Raise average container fill from 71% to 80%

findings.impact: No aggregate, event, or invariant represents a guaranteed departure slot. Invoicing's only invariant ties a line to a cleared declaration, which does not express the premium at all. The 71%->80% fill goal has no invariant or metric owner either.

findings.title: Invoicing carries a 128-attribute entity and five aggregates, three of them modelling tax rules

evidence.invoicing_note: Grown over eleven years. Three of the five aggregates exist to model VAT variations across the nine ports; two were added when the Finnish tax rules changed in 2024.

business_classification.differentiation: **no** — *"nobody has ever chosen us because of our invoices"*

evidence.customs_note: Two commercial customs platforms cover all nine ports; we integrate with neither.

customs_classification.differentiation: no — required, and two vendors already do it well

findings.impact: Both of the heaviest custom builds are capabilities the business itself rates as non-differentiating, and both have off-the-shelf answers (VAT engines; the two commercial customs platforms already covering all nine ports). No build-vs-buy decision is recorded.
